_schema_notes.purpose: Lifestyle, retail, and fashion brand dating signals. Covers brands associated with casualwear, preppy/collegiate fashion, mass-market retail private labels, and fashion-forward American brands.
_schema_notes.confidence: high = well-documented. medium = generally accepted ±2-3 years. low = rough estimate.

Ralph_Lauren_Polo.official_name: Polo Ralph Lauren / Ralph Lauren Corporation
Ralph_Lauren_Polo.notes: Ralph Lauren brand founded 1967 in New York. Originally sold neckties. The polo player logo was introduced in the 1970s. Chaps Ralph Lauren sub-brand launched 1978. Polo Sport line launched 1993.

founding_bound.description: Any Ralph Lauren or Polo by Ralph Lauren label
founding_bound.notes: Ralph Lauren brand did not exist before 1967.

polo_player_logo.description: Polo player on horseback logo on label or garment
polo_player_logo.notes: The polo player design appears on Ralph Lauren tags beginning in the 1970s (approximately 1972+).

polo_by_ralph_lauren_text.notes: First labels were simple with 'Polo by Ralph Lauren' text, often embroidered in white on navy blue.

chaps_ralph_lauren.notes: Chaps Ralph Lauren was created in 1978 as a diffusion line in response to the counterfeit market. The label was used through the late 1990s.

polo_sport.description: Label reads 'Polo Sport' or 'Polo Sport Ralph Lauren'

ralph_lauren_made_usa.description: Polo/Ralph Lauren label reads 'Made in U.S.A.'
ralph_lauren_made_usa.notes: Polo produced more domestically in its earlier decades. Made in USA Polo suggests generally pre-1995.

Lacoste_Izod.official_name: Lacoste (licensed to Izod/David Crystal in US)
Lacoste_Izod.notes: Lacoste founded by Rene Lacoste in France, 1933. US market entered via licensing: 1952 agreement with David Crystal Company (also owned Izod), formalized with Izod licensing to manufacture in the US from 1966. The Lacoste/Izod relationship ended in 1992. Key for dating: labels reading 'Izod Lacoste' or 'Lacoste Made in USA by Izod' indicate specific US manufacture window.

izod_lacoste_combined.description: Label reads 'Izod Lacoste' or combines both brand names
izod_lacoste_combined.notes: Izod licensed Lacoste for US manufacturing from 1966. The relationship ended in 1992. Combined Izod/Lacoste label is a tight 1966-1992 window for US-made Lacoste.

izod_lacoste_early_us.description: US-market Lacoste label with David Crystal or Izod reference
izod_lacoste_early_us.notes: David Crystal began importing/distributing Lacoste in the US from 1952 (formal agreement). US manufacture began 1966.

lacoste_without_izod.description: Lacoste label with no Izod reference (post-1992 US)
lacoste_without_izod.notes: After the Izod relationship ended in 1992, US Lacoste labels dropped the Izod name.

Gap.notes: Founded by Donald and Doris Fisher in San Francisco in 1969. Originally sold only Levi's jeans. Started producing own-label clothing in 1974. Logo changed from lowercase black text to blue box with white capital letters in 1986.

gap_original_logo_lowercase.description: Gap logo in all lowercase black text ('the gap') on white/light background
gap_original_logo_lowercase.notes: Gap's 1969-1986 logo featured all-lowercase black text on white. Changed to blue box with capitalized white text in 1986.

gap_blue_box_logo.description: Gap logo in blue box with white capitalized 'GAP' text
gap_blue_box_logo.notes: Blue box logo introduced 1986 and still in use (with brief failed rebranding attempt in 2010 quickly reverted).

gap_own_label_start.description: Gap-branded clothing label (not Levi's or other third-party)
gap_own_label_start.notes: Gap sold only Levi's through 1973. Own-brand Gap clothing labels begin in 1974.

Banana_Republic_Original.official_name: Banana Republic Travel & Safari Clothing Company (original)
Banana_Republic_Original.notes: Founded 1978 by Mel and Patricia Ziegler in Mill Valley, California as an army surplus import business with a safari/travel theme. Acquired by Gap Inc. in 1983. Original safari/travel concept phased out by 1988 when founders left; fully gone by 1990. The original Banana Republic (1978-1988) is a very distinct vintage proposition from the modern preppy brand.

safari_travel_era.description: Label reads 'Banana Republic Travel & Safari Clothing Co.' or similar safari-era branding
safari_travel_era.notes: The original 'Travel & Safari Clothing Co.' branding ran from 1978 until the Zieglers left in 1988. This is the highly collectible vintage Banana Republic era.

gap_acquisition_era.description: Banana Republic after Gap acquisition (corporate Banana Republic feel, no safari theme)
gap_acquisition_era.notes: Gap acquired Banana Republic in 1983 but kept original management through 1988. Post-1990 Banana Republic has no safari identity.

Abercrombie_Fitch_Original.official_name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (original outdoor/sporting goods brand)
Abercrombie_Fitch_Original.notes: IMPORTANT: There are two distinct Abercrombie & Fitch identities. The ORIGINAL A&F (1892-1977) was a prestigious outdoor sporting goods retailer with celebrity clientele (Teddy Roosevelt, Hemingway, Amelia Earhart). It went bankrupt in 1977. The MODERN A&F (1988-present) is a teen fashion brand revived by Limited Brands with no connection to the outdoor heritage. Vintage A&F clothing from before 1977 is completely different in character and value from modern A&F.

original_af_1892_1977.description: A&F label in heavyweight canvas/twill with bold serif font, no ampersand in early versions, 'EST. 1892' reference
original_af_1892_1977.notes: Original A&F went bankrupt in 1977. Labels from this era feature heavy woven construction, 'ABERCROMBIE & FITCH' in serif font. Often sewn into necklines or waistbands. This is a completely different brand identity from modern A&F.

modern_af_teen_fashion.description: Modern A&F label (soft paper tags, fashion branding, moose logo)
modern_af_teen_fashion.notes: Limited Brands (now L Brands) revived A&F as a teen fashion retailer in 1988. Modern A&F has paper tags, moose branding, and no outdoor heritage connection.

Tommy_Hilfiger.notes: Founded 1985. Rapidly grew in the 1990s through hip-hop culture adoption.

founding_bound.notes: Tommy Hilfiger brand did not exist before 1985.
Nautica brand did not exist before 1983.
Calvin Klein brand did not exist before 1968.

Members_Only.official_name: Members Only (Europe Craft Imports / Glenoit Mills)
Members_Only.notes: Members Only jacket became a cultural phenomenon in the early 1980s. Peak cultural relevance 1981-1988.

peak_era.description: Members Only jacket (especially cafe/racer-style with epaulettes)
peak_era.notes: Members Only's cultural peak was early-to-mid 1980s. Garments from this era are the most collectible.

Izod.notes: The Izod name came from a London tailoring firm. David Crystal Inc. acquired the Izod brand in 1938. David Crystal also held the Lacoste license from 1952-1992. After the Lacoste license ended, Izod continued as an independent preppy brand under various ownership.

izod_david_crystal.description: Label references David Crystal or Izod by David Crystal
izod_david_crystal.notes: David Crystal Inc. held the Izod name from 1938.

izod_lacoste_license.description: Label reads 'Izod Lacoste' or similar combined branding
izod_lacoste_license.notes: Izod manufactured Lacoste under license 1966-1992. See Lacoste_Izod entry.

izod_post_lacoste.notes: Post-1992, Izod operated independently. The standalone Izod brand continued but without Lacoste association.
